messages:
maria: Heads-up — we've had three nodes in us-west-2 show transient Xid/ECC noise over the last 36h. DCGM exporter is firing alerts and a couple of pods got evicted, then came back once the card cooled. Thinking we should formalize a proactive drain + debounce policy for flaky cards instead of pager storms. Thoughts?

kai: Can you paste the alert text and the prom query? are these Xid errors or ECC counts?

maria: alert payload from infra-bot: "GPU_ECC_RATE high on node-gpu-17 (card0) — 42 ECCs in 10m". It's mixed: some true ECC (single-bit/other) and some Xid 31 spikes. PromQL we currently use is pretty naive: `sum by (instance,gpu) (dcgm_gpu_ecc_count_total{job=\"dcgm\"})` with an increase() rule.

jamal: That increase() over short windows is noisy. We should debounce and classify. Proposal:
- Recording rule to get rate per card
- Alert if rate > threshold AND >= N Xid events in M minutes
- Longer `for:` on alert (15m) and group by node to avoid per-gpu fanout

anya: +1 for longer for:. Also we need a documented drain playbook: cordon -> drain (evict) -> annotate node with `gpu/last-flaky=<ts>` -> auto-schedule a replace if it happens > 2x in 7d. Some notes on safe drain: use `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` and ensure we don't evict critical long-running jobs.

maria: sketch of the prometheus bits:
```yaml
# recording rule: per-card rate over 5m
- record: infra:dcgm_ecc_rate:5m
  expr: increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_count_total{job=\"dcgm\"}[5m])

# alert rule (draft)
- alert: GPU_FLAKY_CARD
  expr: infra:dcgm_ecc_rate:5m > 10
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: "High ECC/Xid rate on {{ $labels.instance }}/gpu{{ $labels.gpu }}"
    runbook: "https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-flaky-card"
```

kai: That looks sensible. Two tweaks:
1) Use `increase` only for ECC counters; for Xid we have a gauge-ish exporter metric `dcgm_xid_events_total` — treat Xid>0 as a health flag and require >=3 in 1h to escalate.
2) Group alerts by `node` label and use `max` across GPUs to avoid four pages if card0/1 both noisy.

jamal: Agree. Also add a recording rule for `gpu_flaky_score` combining normalized ECC + Xid counts and moving average to avoid single-sample blips. Example PromQL: `avg_over_time((increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_count_total[5m]) + increase(dcgm_xid_events_total[5m])*3)[30m:])`

anya: Playbook snippet to put in runbook:
```bash
# quick triage
kubectl get nodes -l cloud=us-west-2 -o wide | grep node-gpu-17
ssh node-gpu-17 -- sudo nvidia-smi -q | egrep -i "xid|ecc"
# cordon + drain (staging first)
kubectl cordon node-gpu-17
kubectl drain node-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# annotate node for replacement tracking
kubectl annotate node node-gpu-17 gpu.flaky=true gpu.flaky-count=1 --overwrite
```

infra-bot: [alert] GPU_FLAKY_CARD fired for node-gpu-17 (card0) at 2026-03-17T18:22:14Z :wave:

maria: Plan I propose:
- jamal: open PR to update recording rules + new flaky_score rule (test in staging) — due EOD Thu
- kai: run retrospective query against last 30d to tune thresholds and provide false-positive rate — due Mon
- anya: draft drain/replace playbook + add annotation/label conventions to runbook — due next Wed
- infra team: roll alert with `for:15m`, group by node; switch paging to SEV2 for now, escalation to SEV1 at repeat event within 24h

kai: Will run queries. Quick PromQL to start: `sum by(node) (increase(dcgm_xid_events_total[1h]))` and `sum by (node) (increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_count_total[1h]))`.

jamal: I'll make the PR and include a staging rule that flips on a test metric so we can validate debounce without touching prod alerting.

anya: Add a note to prevent automatic `kubectl drain` in prod unless owner/SE review; for now keep drain manual + annotation + auto-replace only after 2 occurrences.

maria: Sounds good. If no objections I'll kick this off and tag owners. @jamal @kai @anya please update the tasks in the infra board. :thumbsup:

kai: 👍

jamal: on it, thanks

anya: copying this into the runbook draft now
